GOL — Changing the Game for Good

Sport is a vehicle
for people's dreams.

GOL exists to put that vehicle in the hands of the youth and families who need it most — starting on the courts of PPR communities in Malaysia, and building outward from there. Sport breaks down barriers. It builds spirit, skills, and character. It brings people together — and it can be the start of a better life.

The Big Idea

There's a court in every PPR.
Nobody sees it anymore.

Concrete. Faded lines. A goalpost with no net, or no goalpost at all. It's been there for twenty years. Everyone walks past it.

That court is a promise that was made and quietly forgotten. Public housing was meant to come with public life — spaces where community happens, where kids have somewhere to go, something to belong to. Somewhere along the way, the "life" part got dropped.

GOL goes back to that court. Not to tear it down — to activate what's already there. A goal. A coach. A reason to show up on Tuesday and Thursday.

Why GOL, Why Now

This isn't a new direction.
It's where it all started.

“Sixteen years in Malaysian sport, three continents, one organisation built and sold, a national grassroots programme, and a seat at the table with FAM and the Ministry of Youth & Sports — all of it traces back to a PPR court.”

Samuel Siew
Founder, GOL
The Beginning

A "yes" to a futsal carnival

It started small — saying yes to help out as a referee at a futsal carnival in a PPR community. No title, no plan, no programme. Just showing up on a Saturday.

The community kept calling back. Saturday after Saturday, the same court, the same kids — and slowly, a routine became a relationship.

2010 — early community football programme at a PPR court in the Klang Valley.
The Opportunity

London called — because the work was already real

What happened on those courts didn't go unnoticed. It led to a coaching opportunity with a Premier League community programme, and eventually, a one-month placement in London as one of two Southeast Asian representatives on an English FA International Coaching course.

The opportunity wasn't separate from the PPR work. It was the PPR work, recognised on a global stage.

Premier Skills community coaching — the programme that connected PPR courts to an international stage.
The Proof

Five PPR programmes. Then the rest of the journey.

Coming back from London wasn't the end of the chapter — it was confidence to go deeper. Five legacy PPR community sports programmes were built between 2012 and 2018. Then came Dream Village Football Academy — Malaysia's first social enterprise football academy, scaled from zero to 171 players.

FAM came knocking next. Then the Ministry of Youth & Sports. Then Courtsite, scaled from 64 to 350+ venues and 630,000 users. Then Momentum.

Every step after the PPR courts was built because of them — not instead of them. GOL is the moment the loop closes: taking everything built since, and bringing it home.

Mission

Make sport safer, smarter, and more accessible — starting with the communities that need it most.

GOL uses sport as the entry point to unlock digital skills, leadership, and opportunity for youth and families living in PPR public housing communities across Malaysia.

Vision

By 2030, every PPR community has a safe, smart, active court — and a real pathway forward.

GOL aims to be Southeast Asia's leading model for community-based sport-to-digital empowerment, with the Klang Valley pilot as the proof point for replication across public housing communities in Malaysia, Indonesia, and the Philippines.

The Model

Three layers. One circular flow.

Learn, play, connect, empower — repeat. The same circular motif in GOL's brand identity describes exactly how the programme works on the ground. Sport opens the door. Community keeps it open. Digital skills are what walks through it — and the cycle repeats with every new season.

The Loop

Sport

Weekly football & futsal on existing PPR courts — the entry point every kid already understands.

Built on what's already there

GOL doesn't ask for new land. It reactivates existing PPR courts — smarter goals, better lighting, simple infrastructure upgrades — so the same concrete that's sat empty for years becomes safe, durable, and ready for daily use.

Accessibility

Every programme is free for participants, embedded directly in the community — no membership, no equipment cost, no barrier to walk onto the court.

Durability

Equipment and infrastructure chosen for tropical heat, monsoon rain, and heavy daily use — built to last seasons, not weeks.

Safety

Child safeguarding policy, trained and vetted coaches, and insured sessions from day one — every parent can know exactly who's on that court.

Innovation

A digital layer — AI literacy, basic usage data, outcome tracking — built in from the pilot stage, not bolted on later.

What Makes GOL Different

The first community sports network in Malaysia built digital from day one.

Every GOL court isn't just a place to play — it's a data point. Every session isn't just an activity — it's measurable, trackable, and adoptable. This is the layer that makes GOL fundable, scalable, and genuinely first-of-its-kind in Malaysia's grassroots sports landscape.

01 · SMART INFRASTRUCTURE

Solar-powered, sensor-ready courts

Solar lighting extends play into the evening. Lightweight cameras support safety monitoring and basic usage detection — built for Malaysia's heat, humidity, and monsoon seasons from day one.

02 · PDPA-COMPLIANT DATA

Privacy-first participation tracking

Every participant is counted, not identified. Attendance, usage patterns, and programme reach are tracked in full compliance with Malaysia's Personal Data Protection Act — building trust with families and regulators alike.

03 · OPEN ACCESS, OPEN DATA

A platform, not a silo

Court availability, programme schedules, and participation data are designed to be visible — to communities, to local councils, and eventually to other NGOs who want to run programmes on GOL infrastructure.

From impact story to investment dashboard

For sponsors and adopters, GOL doesn't just deliver a feel-good update — it delivers a dashboard. Number of sessions run, youth reached, hours of safe play unlocked, digital workshops completed — all tied back to the specific court, programme, or community a sponsor has adopted.

This turns CSR spend into something closer to an investment with visible, trackable returns — and gives corporate partners exactly the kind of reporting their ESG teams need.

  • Adopt-a-Court — a sponsor's name, brand, or memory attached to a specific reactivated PPR court, with usage data reported back quarterly.
  • Real-time participation data — sessions run, attendance, and programme completion, visible on a simple dashboard.
  • Solar & safety infrastructure — lighting and basic camera coverage that doubles as both a safety feature and a usage-data source.
  • Replicable, exportable model — every court built on GOL's framework can be measured the same way, anywhere in Malaysia or the region.

Pro ↔ Grassroots: bringing athletes home

Malaysia's professional and former athletes came from somewhere — often, from communities just like the ones GOL serves. GOL creates the bridge for them to give back, directly, to where they're from.

FOR ATHLETES

Adopt your hometown court

Former and current professional athletes are invited to adopt a PPR court in their hometown — lending their name, running occasional clinics, and inspiring the next generation from the community they came from.

FOR COMMUNITIES

A pathway back, and a pathway up

Kids on GOL courts see a realistic version of themselves in the athletes who visit — people who started on the same concrete, in the same kind of community, and made it.

The Operating Plan

Prove it. Fund it. Scale it.

Money and energy go to communities first — paperwork second. Each phase is designed to be earned by the one before it.

2026–2027 · Prove the Model

Three PPR pilots, done well

  • Register GOL as a Society — fast, low-cost, focused
  • Convene founding Exco & confirm Patron
  • Launch in 3 PPR sites across the Klang Valley
  • Weekly football/futsal + first digital literacy series
  • Recruit & train resident youth as Playmaker coaches
  • Secure first seed grant (Yayasan Hasanah Micro Grant)
2028–2029 · Build the Evidence

Formalise & fund the foundation

  • Convert to Foundation (CLBG), Section 44(6) status
  • Expand to 5+ PPR sites across Selangor & KL
  • Publish first verified Impact Report
  • Multi-year Yayasan Hasanah Grant
  • First corporate ESG anchor sponsor
  • Pilot first smart court infrastructure upgrade
2030+ · Scale Nationally

Malaysia's reference model for community sport

  • 10+ PPR sites across multiple states
  • Formal partnerships with state governments
  • National corporate & ESG sponsor network
  • Earned-income arm reduces grant dependency
  • 10,000+ youth reached nationwide

Why This Matters — To Builders of Nations

An anchor investment in Kuala Lumpur
becomes an ecosystem.

Every major institution that has shaped Malaysia's social fabric — in education, in healthcare, in community development — started with one decision to invest in one place, then let the model prove itself before it scaled.

GOL asks for the same kind of belief. Not a national rollout on day one — a foundation, proven in the Klang Valley, built with the rigour and evidence that turns a single pilot into a model worth replicating.

For a partner thinking in terms of ecosystems rather than transactions, GOL's PPR pilots are the seed. What grows from them — community trust, youth leadership, a digital-skills pipeline, and a replicable infrastructure model — is the return.

THE LOGIC

One pilot. A provable model.

Three PPR sites in the Klang Valley, run to a high standard, with measured outcomes from day one — the evidence base that justifies everything that comes after.

THE MULTIPLIER

From KL outward

A proven KL model becomes the template for every PPR community in Malaysia — and the reference point for similar public housing challenges across Southeast Asia.

THE RETURN

Measured, lasting impact

Youth participation, digital skills uptake, community safety and cohesion — tracked from the first pilot, reportable against SDG and ESG frameworks from year one.

Global Partnerships

Malaysia first. The playbook is global.

GOL's model — reactivating underused public courts with smarter, safer infrastructure and a community programme on top — has precedent.

In New York City, retractable goal systems have been installed directly into NYCHA public housing courts, turning basketball blacktops into multi-sport spaces in seconds — without requiring any new land. The parallel to Malaysia's PPR courts is direct.

As GOL's pilots prove out, exploring infrastructure partnerships with organisations already operating in this space — including conversations already underway in the US sports-tech ecosystem — forms part of the long-term roadmap for bringing proven hardware models into the Malaysian and Southeast Asian context.

PRECEDENT

Public housing, reactivated

NYCHA (New York City Housing Authority) courts upgraded with retractable multi-sport goal systems — proof that minimal infrastructure change can reactivate underused public space at scale.

THE OPPORTUNITY

SEA is untapped

No equivalent deployment exists yet in Southeast Asia. GOL's PPR pilots position Malaysia — and GOL — as the natural first mover and regional partner for proven sport-infrastructure models entering SEA.
